metadata.methods_description: EEG data were collected using ear-EEG equipment, with the first two recordings including concurrent polysomnography (PSG) measurements. For the initial two subjects, recording equipment was mounted in the afternoon by researchers; for remaining subjects, equipment was self-mounted immediately before sleep. All recordings took place in subjects' home environments. Subjects marked key timepoints (recording start, electrode test start, bedtime, lights-out, recording end) using trigger buttons on the equipment.

citation_details.title: Ear-EEG sleep monitoring data sets
citation_details.author: Kaare B. Mikkelsen, Yousef R. Tabar, Laura Birch, Simon L. Kappel, Christian Bech Christensen, Lars Dalskov Mosgaard, Marit Otto, Martin Christian Hemmsen, Mike Lind Rank, Preben Kidmose
citation_details.abstract: Here we present data from two studies, both of which had the purpose of investigating the potential of using electroencephalograms measured from the ear ('ear-EEG') for sleep monitoring in a home environment. In total, 320 nights were recorded. All nights were recorded with ear-EEG, and some were also recorded using scalp-EEG and/or wristworn actigraphy. All subjects were recorded multiple times. To our knowledge, this is the most extensive open access data set available for mobile EEG development, and possibly also the best open access dataset for studying repeated sleep monitoring on individuals. We describe the details of each data set, including data quality measures, and compare the sleep scoring performance to a previously published dataset.
